name: 599. A provider added at runtime answers to its prefix on its first request (prefix-on-add)
description:
TXE-7501 / PR #339. A custom provider added through POST /api/providers is built by core on its first request, and its name became a known model prefix only then. So the first request naming it, "<provider>/model", parsed to no provider: the model catalog sent it to whichever provider's wildcard key claimed the model string, and the new provider was reached at best as a fallback.

Each row creates its own run-scoped keyless OpenAI-backed provider whose base URL is the provider error fixture, and sends the very first request on it as "<provider>/upstream-ok~<run tag>". Keyless, because adding a key through /keys builds the provider in core first and hides the bug. The gateway config of the fixture group has many wildcard keys, the condition under which the first request was misrouted. A row pins that the request succeeded on the new provider with the prefix stripped, and, from the fixture's /__hits, that the fixture received the bare model once and never the prefixed one. Row 1 is a chat completion, row 2 the same as a stream. The rows skip themselves outside a fixture run; each deletes its provider, and providers an aborted run left behind are swept after ten minutes.
